purpose: Independent practice of B2.5 (multiplication as repeated equal groups). Captures formative evidence on group-building and equation writing.
student_learning_goal: I can show a multiplication problem as repeated equal groups, draw the groups, and write the multiplication equation.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can show a multiplication problem as repeated equal groups, draw the groups, and write the multiplication equation.
header.character_watermark: Mae the Multiplier in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Each scene shows N baskets with M kittens each. Write the repeated addition AND the multiplication equation.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Six basket scenes in a 2x3 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Six basket scenes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 3-column grid. Each scene ~2.2in × 1.5in. Pre-fills: B1 — 4 baskets of 3 kittens; B2 — 5 baskets of 2 kittens; B3 — 3 baskets of 4 kittens; B4 — 6 baskets of 2 kittens; B5 — 4 baskets of 4 kittens; B6 — 5 baskets of 3 kittens. Below each scene, two equation lines: 'Repeated addition: ___' and 'Multiplication: ___ × ___ = ___'.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; six baskets in 2x3 grid.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P1_SIX_BASKETS: keywords (baskets, kittens) name what the scenes show.

parts.student_instructions: Each array shows R rows and C columns of dots. Write the multiplication equation.
parts.visual_layout: Middle. Four array grids in a 2x2 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Four array grids in B&W line-art, 2-row × 2-column grid. Each array ~2.5in × 2in. Pre-fills: A1 — 3 rows × 4 columns of dots (3×4=12); A2 — 4 rows × 5 columns (4×5=20); A3 — 6 rows × 2 columns (6×2=12); A4 — 5 rows × 3 columns (5×3=15). Below each array, the multiplication equation line.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P2_FOUR_ARRAYS: keywords (array, rows) name what the grids show.

parts.student_instructions: For each multiplication problem, draw the equal groups OR the array.

image_placeholders.description: Three blank rectangular drawing boxes in B&W line-art, stacked vertically, each ~7in × 1.5in with light-grey solid outline. Above each box, a multiplication problem: 5 × 4, 3 × 6, 4 × 5. The child draws either equal groups or an array.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P3_THREE_BUILDS: keywords (build, draw) name what the boxes ask for.

parts.answer_key: 5×4=20: 5 groups of 4 OR 5 rows × 4 columns. 3×6=18: 3 groups of 6 OR 3 rows × 6 columns. 4×5=20: 4 groups of 5 OR 4 rows × 5 columns.

parts.student_instructions: Where do you see equal groups in real life? Draw and write 1-2 examples.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box for drawing and writing real-life examples.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular drawing box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in, with light-grey solid outline. Mae thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner of the box (~1in tall).
image_placeholders.placement: Bottom of the page; spans full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P4_REAL_LIFE_BOX: keywords (real-life, groups) name what the box is for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any plausible real-life equal-group: '6 packs of 4 juice boxes = 24', '3 rows of 5 chairs = 15', '4 boxes of 6 crayons = 24'.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw a multiplication problem of your own — 7 × 3 — using either equal groups or an array.
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Use Part 1 as evidence of B2.5 group-building flexibility — children who write both forms are at L4. Watch for Part 2 children who reverse rows-and-columns (writing 4×3 for a 3-row × 4-column array) — flag for the row-vs-column reteach.
